Two findings emitted below.

evidence: Multiple AI list endpoints forward a caller-controlled `?limit=` straight into a SQL `LIMIT $n` with NO upper-bound clamp, unlike the rest of the codebase which caps it. Concrete route-layer sites: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/ai/sessions.rs:101 (`query.limit.unwrap_or(50)`), sessions.rs:205, sessions.rs:924, sessions.rs:997; ai/equipment.rs:203, ai/equipment.rs:297, ai/equipment.rs:379; ai/llm.rs:1448; ai/voice.rs:308. Each passes `query.limit.unwrap_or(N)` unchanged to a repo method.

Repo layer confirms no clamp downstream either: backend/crates/db/src/repositories/ai_chat.rs:133-163 `list_user_sessions(executor, user_id, limit, offset)` binds `limit` directly to `LIMIT $2 OFFSET $3` (line 154) with no `.min()`. backend/crates/db/src/repositories/equipment.rs list_maintenance (LIMIT $3 OFFSET $4, ~line 326) is the same shape -- no clamp anywhere in the grep for `.min(` in that file.

Contrast (proof this is an inconsistency, not a house style): backend/crates/db/src/repositories/listing.rs:136 clamps `let limit = query.limit.unwrap_or(20).min(100);`, and route-layer admin handlers clamp too -- routes/admin/users.rs:58 `.min(100)`, routes/admin/audit.rs:235 `.min(500)`, routes/admin/users_lifecycle.rs:273 `.clamp(1,100)`. reality-server even has a dedicated regression suite (listings_pagination_clamp_tests.rs). The AI routes missed the same guard.

Impact: an authenticated caller can request `?limit=100000000` and force an unbounded result-set materialization on tenant-scoped tables (chat sessions/messages, equipment maintenance, LLM request log) -> DB scan + Rust Vec allocation resource-exhaustion / latency-amplification (self-scoped DoS). A negative limit reaches Postgres as a bind error -> 500 rather than a clean 400. Fix (cloud-landable, no migration): add `.clamp(1, 100)` (or a shared `PageLimit` newtype) at each route site before the repo call, or clamp inside the repo methods to mirror listing.rs:136.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/auth/mod.rs:1001 -- in the refresh-token path, when a user is found but `user.status != "active"`, the defense-in-depth revoke is fire-and-forgotten: `let _ = state.session_repo.revoke_token(stored_token.id).await;`. A failure to revoke the still-live refresh token of a just-deactivated/suspended account is silently discarded (no log, no metric).

This is inconsistent with the sibling revoke 9 lines below at auth/mod.rs:1010-1013 (the normal rotation path), which does `if let Err(e) = ... revoke_token(...) { tracing::error!(error = %e, "Failed to revoke old refresh token"); }`. The security-relevant branch (revoking a deactivated account's token) is the one that logs nothing.

Severity is low because the `user.status` gate re-runs on every refresh so a non-revoked token cannot mint a new access token while inactive; the concern is auditability/observability of a security operation on deactivated accounts, and inconsistency with the adjacent path. Fix: replace the `let _ =` with the same `if let Err(e) = ... { tracing::warn!(error = %e, user_id = %user_id, "Failed to revoke token for deactivated account"); }` shape used at line 1010.
